claim_ceiling: The two provenance-traceable ordinary-light witnesses show a tiny low-contrast dark trace within the reddish-painted west tuber of f99v plant [3,4], but they do not resolve whether it is deliberate writing, how many characters it contains, or whether it belongs to Voynich script or a plain alphabet. It therefore does not supply a second authenticated Voynich-script under-paint note and establishes no colour, word, sound, language, cipher, plaintext, meaning, or translation.

prior_human_annotation.local_comment: Apparent letters on West tuber of plant <f99v>[3,4]. Tiny, but visible in BLI04 under the reddish paint. Is it real?

visual_observations.observation: Both ordinary-light witnesses contain a localized low-contrast dark trace within the reddish-painted west tuber of plant [3,4].
The trace is far weaker and less sharply bounded than the ordinary Voynich labels and paragraph writing surrounding the plant row.
The scans do not distinguish deliberate ink beneath paint from pigment variation, abrasion, parchment texture, or another incidental mark.
The trace does not yield a stable character count or segmentation shared across the two witnesses.
Neither a plain p/r reading nor the older qo??? suggestion is recoverable independently from the pixels.
The trace cannot be classified as Voynich-style or plain-alphabet writing at this resolution.
